_doc: CC-CEDICT lines (verbatim from the shipped dictionary, CC BY-SA 4.0, MDBG) and a word level list (levels-pack shaped: name, entries of form and marked reading), and texts with the tokens /api/segment must produce over them with the rules of zh.json: surface, reading (the match's reading, pinyin as the server sends it) and function (true only for a function word; absent otherwise). cases run with the level list installed, withoutLevels without it. greedy, when present, is what greedy longest match produced (the bug). Go: server/internal/segment/contract_zh_test.go; web: lib/features/reader/functionWords.contract.test.ts reads the tokens' function flags.

cases.name: issue: 那 is nà (not nā, the surname line); 那是 is not on the list but 那 and 是 are, so it splits
issue: 着 after a verb is the function word zhe (not zhāo); 看 is kàn (the line with the most everyday glosses, not kān)
issue: 学得很好 is 学｜得｜很｜好: 得很 is not on the list, its parts are; 得 is the function word de
issue: 打 is dǎ (the listed entry's everyday line, not the loanword dá)
issue: 有时间 is 有｜时间, not 有时｜间 (间 is listed only through 时间, so it costs as unlisted)
issue: 在教室 is 在｜教室, not 在教｜室 (在教 is not on the list, 在 and 教 are)
issue: 不是 and 这不 split into listed words
issue: 一个 splits into 一｜个
issue: 中国人 splits into 中国｜人
issue: 明天见 splits into 明天｜见
a listed compound stays whole; 吗 is a function word
listed compounds stay whole
a listed three-character word stays whole
an unlisted compound stays whole when a part is unlisted (熊 is not on the list)
吧 and 了 are function words (ba, le)
地 after an adjective is the function word de
长 reads cháng (the readings table): CC-CEDICT's zhǎng line has as many glosses
在地上 is 在｜地上: 地 is a function word that counts as the last part of a compound only (在地 splits; 地上 stays the noun, not 地*｜上)
没 reads méi (the readings table): CC-CEDICT's mò line has more glosses; 还 is hái
Latin letters are no token

withoutLevels.name: without a level list nothing is split: 那是 stays one token
without a level list the readings still come from the rules and CC-CEDICT's glosses
without a level list 打 is dǎ (more everyday glosses than dá)
without a level list 得很 stays one token (nothing tells it apart)
